thread:
alex: Quick follow-up from the reconciliation RFC — sketching a pragmatic protocol that covers active/active + residency constraints. Wanted to get quick opinions before I write up an RFC addendum. :thinking:

maria: TL;DR?

alex: Short version: hybrid approach — lease-backed primary hints + anti-entropy background reconciliation. Key goals: (1) avoid split-write finality, (2) respect tenant residency flags (EU/US), (3) bounded stale reads during failover.

josh: Sounds reasonable. How do you detect/avoid split-brain when proxies disagree on lease state?

alex: Two things: (A) lease holders publish a signed lease claim to control-plane with monotonic lease_epoch, (B) proxy-to-proxy handshakes use `X-Region-Lease: <epoch, holder, sig>` header. If mismatch, proxy prefers control-plane canonical state and rejects conflicting writes until resolution.

samantha: Can we see a tiny example of the handshake header?

alex: Sure — rough example:
```
POST /v1/infer
Host: inference.redwood.internal
X-Region: eu-west
X-Region-Lease: epoch=42;holder=proxy-eu-1;sig=MEUCIQ...
X-Tenant-Residency: eu_only
```
Proxy checks signature, epoch monotonicity, and control-plane TTL. If signature invalid -> 412 + `conflicting-lease` header.

leo: What about cache KV/contexts? If proxy A accepts some prefix tokens then fails over to proxy B, do we replay?

alex: Plan: (1) prefix/KV caching stays best-effort and tagged with lease_epoch; (2) failover path reads `lease_epoch` and rejects cached prefix if epoch < control-plane epoch - 1; (3) if prefixes are rejected we fallback to re-run the prompt (with an idempotency token) and instrument token-cost delta. We want fallback to be explicit, not implicit silent divergence.

maria: That re-run has cost implications — we should add an explicit metric and billing tag like `replay_reason=lease-mismatch`. Also feature-flag the re-run on Dedicated for a period.

josh: How long do we let an operator extend stale leases? Need a graceful window to avoid thrash during region flaps.

alex: Proposal: two time constants: `lease_grace = 30s` ephemeral for operator ops; `eviction_grace = 5m` for automated operatorless eviction. Leases renew frequently (10s) but control-plane enforces max age.

sre-bot: alert: region eu-west experienced 18s lease renewal jitter at 2026-02-12T09:12Z. See runbook #geo-lease-jitter.

samantha: For residency we must be strict: if `X-Tenant-Residency: eu_only` and request lands outside EU, we should route to resident region or fail with 451-like response. Do we plan that?

alex: Yes — routing layer consults residency flag before attempting fallback. If no resident capacity we return `451 residency_unavailable` and trigger a high-priority capacity-fill workflow. We avoid soft-fallback to non-resident regions for PII-sensitive tenants.

leo: Cross-region reconciliation itself — anti-entropy window size? full scans are expensive.

alex: Anti-entropy: delta-first sync using vector clocks per-tenant plus a periodic compact sweep. Sync stream carries `ops {seq, tombstone, lease_epoch}`. We keep per-tenant last-synced vector. If vector gap > threshold -> enqueue a full rehydrate (rate-limited).

maria: Vector clocks per-tenant might explode for high-traffic tenants. Consider seq ranges with checkpoints instead of full vectors.

alex: Agreed — implement as sharded checkpoints: (tenant_id, shard_id) -> last_seq. We'll note that in the addendum.

josh: Operator UX: we need a single control-plane view that shows conflicting leases, pending replays, and residency violations. Without that we'll get paged at 3am.

alex: Will add three console panels: Lease map, Replay queue, Residency gaps. Also add a `reconcile_reason` tag to logs.

samantha: Edge-case: concurrent write that modifies tenant-residency flag. How do we prevent races?

alex: Residency changes are control-plane only with a change-id; proxies readpinned to previous residency until change is globally accepted (two-phase commit style) — forcing a brief quiesce for that tenant. We'll document expected service disruption window (seconds).

leo: Anything we should simulate in chaos tests?

alex: Yes — a matrix: region-flap + control-plane lag + KV-cache primed + residency-change mid-flap. We want to validate: no silent split-writes, explicit replays, and correct `451` behavior.

maria: I'll add the experiments to the infra backlog. +1 to metrics and feature-flag deployment.

josh: OK, if you put this into an RFC addendum let's call out clear SLO impacts (replay token cost, 451 failures) and a rollback plan. :+1:

alex: Thanks all — I'll draft the addendum and share a link tomorrow. If anyone wants to pair on the implementation plan ping me.

sre-bot: deploybot: addendum draft created at https://docs.internal/rfcs/recon-addendum-2026-02-12 — author alex
